item.title: US Service Sector Expands at a Slower Pace, Hiring Picks Up
item.description: The US service sector expanded in June at a slightly slower pace, but firms boosted payrolls as cost pressures eased.

item.title: Microsoft’s Xbox to Cut 3,200 Jobs, Divest Five Studios in Major Overhaul
item.description: Compulsion and Double Fine studios will become independent; Undead Labs and Ninja Theory will be sold. Xbox will also look to sell or spin out Arkane Studios.

item.title: HSBC’s Kettner Sees Hyperscalers Back in Favor Amid ‘Melt-Up’
item.description: Investors who recently scorned so-called hyperscalers are starting to come back as the companies show they can mint profits while spending hundreds of billions of dollars on artificial-intelligence infrastructure, according to Max Kettner of HSBC Holdings Plc.

item.title: Israel Cuts Interest Rates to the Lowest Level Since 2022
item.description: Israel cut interest rates for a second straight meeting, to the lowest level since late 2022, with a strong currency and moderate inflation expectations outweighing an anticipated pickup in growth.

item.title: BlackRock, Vanguard ETFs Diverge Over 170% AI-Fueled Rally
item.description: For more than a decade, investors could treat the two biggest emerging-market exchange-traded funds as almost interchangeable.

item.title: Container Carriers Eye Return to Red Sea Route
item.description: A.P. Moller-Maersk A/S and Hapag-Lloyd AG signaled confidence about resuming passage through the Red Sea, sending the container carriers’ shares down on expectation a return to the shorter route will ease capacity constraints and temper a surge in shipping rates.

item.title: Lockheed to Buy Ultra Maritime for $3.45 Billion in Sea Push
item.description: Lockheed Martin Corp. agreed to buy naval defense business Ultra Maritime, which focuses on submarine detection systems, for $3.45 billion as the US defense giant broadens its undersea weapons portfolio.

item.title: Broadcom, Apple Extend Tie-Up to 2031 With New Custom Chips
item.description: Broadcom Inc. said that it will provide new custom chips to Apple Inc. in an expanded partnership that now runs through 2031.

item.title: Saudis Slash Main Oil Price to Rare Discount as Market Dives
item.description: Saudi Arabia made big reductions to its main crude oil prices for buyers in Asia, selling barrels at a discount for the first time since it embarked on a price war in 2020, as a surge of global supply heightens competition to find buyers.

item.title: Rogers Pays $3.1 Billion for Full Control of NBA, NHL Teams
item.description: Rogers Communications Inc. agreed to buy the remaining 25% stake in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment Ltd. for C$4.35 billion ($3.1 billion) from billionaire Larry Tanenbaum’s Kilmer Group, taking full ownership of Canada’s largest sports empire.

item.title: Russia Oil Price Falls to Pre-Iran War Level in Blow to Kremlin
item.description: Russia’s flagship crude price has slid to levels seen before the conflict in the Middle East, piling more pressure on Kremlin coffers that are already strained by the invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Return of the Right Sparks Record Inflow to Chile Peso Bonds
item.description: Foreign investors are piling into Chile’s local government debt at the fastest pace on record, attracted by a weaker peso, the prospect of interest rate cuts and the return of a more market-friendly government.

item.title: Europe’s Equity Bankers Bet on Capex Wave to Ride Out IPO Slump
item.description: Record spending on AI infrastructure and power grids is fueling a flurry of capital raises by listed companies, giving bankers one of their busiest starts in years and eclipsing the slowdown of initial public offerings in the region.

item.title: Quant Hedge Funds Extend Worst Run Since 2023 as Momentum Slides
item.description: A violent rotation in the underbelly of a bullish stock market is extending the worst run for quantitative hedge funds since 2023.

item.title: Tech Stocks Rebound as Dip Buyers Pounce on Chip Pullback
item.description: US stocks climbed on Monday as investors jumped on technology shares after the artificial-intelligence trade notched one of its sharpest pullbacks in more than two years.

item.title: Reddit Is Cracking Down on AI Marketing Slop With Its Own AI
item.description: Reddit Inc. is battling a new kind of spam: stealth marketing content created by brands that want to get mentioned by popular artificial intelligence chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini.

item.title: Tencent Seeks to Sell Up to $1.6 Billion Stake in Kuaishou
item.description: Tencent Holdings Ltd. is seeking to raise as much as $1.55 billion in a selldown of part of its stake in short-video app operator Kuaishou Technology through a block trade.

item.title: OPEC+ Emerges From War to Threat of Oil Surplus
item.description: Key members have agreed on another production hike, yet there may be little need for the extra barrels.

item.title: Brookfield’s Data Center Firm Csquare Seeks $1.35 Billion in IPO
item.description: Csquare Inc., a data center company backed by Brookfield Corp., is seeking to raise as much as $1.35 billion in a US initial public offering.

item.title: BOE Confirms Exit of Chief Cashier Ahead of Controversial Banknote Switch
item.description: The Bank of England has announced the departure of its chief cashier Victoria Cleland and named Rhys Phillips as her successor in charge of Britain’s supply of banknotes.

item.title: Sony’s All-Digital PlayStation Strategy Doesn’t Sit Well With Gamers
item.description: The former champion of sharing-friendly policies has changed

item.title: Global Rate Outlook Higher on Trump-Iran War Shock
item.description: The conflict in the Middle East may be subsiding, but the repercussions for central banks around the world are here to stay.

item.title: Trump’s Blue-Collar Base Worry Tariffs Aren’t a Cure-All for Factory Malaise
item.description: The duties Trump imposed on American importers haven’t sparked an industrial renaissance

item.title: Ondas to Buy Autonomous Aircraft Maker DZYNE for $875.8 Million
item.description: Ondas Inc. agreed to buy autonomous aircraft maker DZYNE Technologies in an $875.8 million cash-and stock-deal that positions Ondas as a full-service autonomous defense technology platform.

item.title: Bolivia Moves to Lure $4 Billion Cash Hoard Into Banking System
item.description: Bolivia is taking steps to reintroduce dollar savings accounts to pull greenbacks hoarded under mattresses back into the financial system.

item.title: US Investors Are Finally Getting a Clear Shot at SK Hynix
item.description: Until now, it has been difficult, if not impossible, for American investors to bet on SK Hynix.

item.title: Memory Chipmaker SK Hynix Starts Marketing US Listing
item.description: SK Hynix Inc. kicked off its formal marketing process for its US listing on Monday, as the South Korean chipmaker looks to capitalize on surging investor demand for the high-flying memory-chip sector.

item.title: Standard Bank Warns of Flight From Sovereign Debt as Safety Ebbs
item.description: Investors seeking to insulate their portfolios against turbulence should increasingly look beyond government bonds, which appear to be losing their traditional safe-haven status, according to Standard Bank’s head of G10 strategy.

item.title: Ready for the Future, Ireland Is Also Vulnerable to It
item.description: Ireland may be a bellwether for how an economy can bet its future on technology and lose.

item.title: The Investors Scrambling to Keep SpaceX - and Elon Musk - Out of Their Portfolios
item.description: Christopher Bejnar has spent the last couple of months combing through the fine print of exchange-traded funds, emailing financial advisers and moving money into European stocks – all to keep SpaceX out of his $1 million portfolio.
